title: Ordinary ringed pullback transports stratified perfect local models
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$ and a uniformizer $t$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. On the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] put $C_{n,W}=(R/t^n)_W$ for $n\geq1$ and $B_W=\varprojlim_n C_{n,W}$ with projections $\pi_{W,n}$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Use the coefficient map $c_f:f^{-1}B_Y\to B_X$ characterized by $\pi_{X,n}c_f=c^f_{R/t^n}f^{-1}(\pi_{Y,n})$, where $c^f_{R/t^n}$ is the constant-section structure map [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Let $f_B^*Q=B_X\otimes_{f^{-1}B_Y}f^{-1}Q$ be ordinary module pullback, applied termwise to complexes, and let $P_f=Lf_B^*$ with its canonical K-flat computation counit $\epsilon_Q:P_f[Q]\to[f_B^*Q]$ [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback]. Here $[Q]$ denotes localization of a complex in the ordinary unbounded derived category of module sheaves [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]; tensors are sheaf tensors [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product].

Assume $X,Y$ are noetherian, meaning locally noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact. Let $K\in D(B_Y)$, let $i_i:S_i\hookrightarrow Y$ be a finite constructible locally closed stratification [def-constructible-stratification], and suppose that there are pro-etale covers $\{U_{ia}\to S_i\}_a$ and bounded complexes $L_{ia}^{\bullet}$ of finite projective $R$-modules such that $i_i^*K|_{U_{ia}}\simeq B_{U_{ia}}\otimes_R L_{ia}^{\bullet}$. Finite projective means a direct summand of a finite free module; ordinary exact immersion restriction is meant [lem-sf-immersion-completed-pullback-comparison].

Set $X_i=X\times_Y S_i$, $j_i:X_i\hookrightarrow X$, $f_i:X_i\to S_i$, and $V_{ia}=X_i\times_{S_i}U_{ia}$, with projection $v_{ia}:V_{ia}\to U_{ia}$. After discarding empty $X_i$, the $j_i$ form a finite constructible locally closed stratification of $X$, and $\{V_{ia}\to X_i\}_a$ are pro-etale covers. The coefficient structural maps of the equal composites $fj_i=i_if_i$ agree under the inverse-image composition isomorphisms, as do all their finite projections. The canonical ordinary derived composition and slice-restriction comparisons give
$$j_i^*P_fK\simeq P_{f_i}(i_i^*K),\qquad
(j_i^*P_fK)|_{V_{ia}}\simeq P_{v_{ia}}(B_{U_{ia}}\otimes_R L_{ia}^{\bullet})\simeq B_{V_{ia}}\otimes_R L_{ia}^{\bullet}.$$
The last isomorphism is computed termwise on each bounded finite-projective model: it sends a pulled free basis vector to the same basis vector and restricts by the same idempotent to every finite-projective summand. These are the ordinary ringed comparisons, before taking any completion; no completeness assumption on $P_fK$, no flatness or invertibility of $c_f$, and no separatedness or base-field linearity of $f$ is assumed.

source.place: Proposition 6.6.11 and Remark 6.8.15: base-changed strata, covering slices and finite-projective ordinary pullback models. Agent extraction of original steps 2-3, with the model interfaces used by steps 1 and 4.

proof.text: Apply [lemma-constructible-pullback-stratification] to $f$ and $(i_i)$: the base-changed immersions $j_i$ have pairwise disjoint images $f^{-1}(|S_i|)$ covering $X$. Their images are constructible by [lem-pur-scheme-constructible-preimage], applied to the constructible images of $i_i$. Delete the empty images; this preserves the covering, disjointness and finiteness. Base change each covering family along $f_i$. Its arrows remain weakly etale by [lem-weil-pbc-weakly-etale-composition-base-change] and the family remains fpqc by [lem-galois-fpqc-covering-base-change]. These are precisely the covering conditions in [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], so the $V_{ia}$ give the asserted covers. No finite-type hypothesis on $f$ is used.

source.place: Proposition 6.6.11, base-changing the finite stratification and its local perfect charts; covering base change is Stacks Tags 094U and 022D

proof.text:
For composable scheme maps $T\xrightarrow h W\xrightarrow k Z$, let $\alpha:(kh)^{-1}\simeq h^{-1}k^{-1}$ be the canonical inverse-image compositor. The finite rings $R/t^n$ of [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension] satisfy [lem-trf-constant-coefficient-composition]. Thus, suppressing $\alpha$ in the notation, the defining projection equations give
$$\pi_{T,n}c_hh^{-1}c_k=c^h_nh^{-1}(\pi_{W,n})h^{-1}c_k=c^h_nh^{-1}(c^k_n)h^{-1}k^{-1}(\pi_{Z,n})=c^{kh}_n(kh)^{-1}(\pi_{Z,n})=\pi_{T,n}c_{kh}.$$
Maps into $B_T$ are determined by all these projections, by [def-pur-sheaf-inverse-limit]. This proves equality of the coefficient structural maps for a composite, and proves their equality at each finite projection at the same time. In particular apply this calculation to $fj_i=i_if_i$. It asserts equality of maps and does not require any of the completed coefficient maps to be invertible.

source.place: Tag 03CB, lemma-composition-morphisms-sites, and Tag 0H7J, example-constant-sheaf; elementary projection calculation for the inverse limit

proof.text: For any chart $u:U_{ia}\to S_i$, [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization] identifies $(S_i)_{\mathrm{proet}}/U_{ia}$ with $(U_{ia})_{\mathrm{proet}}$, and identifies the restrictions of every constant ring $R/t^n$ by the identity on constant sections. Limits are sectionwise by [def-pur-sheaf-inverse-limit]; hence the restricted ring $B_{S_i}|_{U_{ia}}$ is $B_{U_{ia}}$, with precisely the restricted finite projections. Do the same on $X_i$ and $V_{ia}$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-localize-ringed-site-morphism] to the base-change functor defining $f_i$. Its localized coefficient map, under these ring identifications, is $c_{v_{ia}}$: at every finite projection both maps are induced by the same constant-section map, so the preceding projection argument identifies them. Thus this localized ringed morphism is the one used to define $P_{v_{ia}}$.

source.place: Tag 04IF, lemma-localize-morphism-ringed-topoi; proetale.tex Tag 09AE localization convention; sectionwise limit identification

proof.text: Use the ordinary unbounded ringed-topos comparison [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons] for $(j_i,f)$ and $(f_i,i_i)$. Step 2 identifies their composite structural maps over the canonical geometric isomorphism associated to $fj_i=i_if_i$, so the specified two-isomorphism transport in that same node identifies $P_{fj_i}$ with $P_{i_if_i}$. The two composition comparisons therefore give $P_{j_i}P_fK\simeq P_{f_i}P_{i_i}K$. Both immersions are locally closed, so [lem-sf-immersion-completed-pullback-comparison] gives ordinary exact $P_{j_i}=j_i^*$ and $P_{i_i}=i_i^*$. This proves the first asserted isomorphism, with no completeness assumption on $K$ or $P_fK$: only the unconditional ordinary-exactness clause of the immersion node is used.

source.place: Tag 0D6D, lemma-derived-pullback-composition; K-flat representative normalization; Bhatt--Scholze Remark 6.8.15 for exact immersion restriction

proof.text: Apply [lem-sbc-ringed-topos-sheaf-slice-derived-comparison] to the ringed morphism $f_i$ and the sheaf $A=h_{U_{ia}}$, a sheaf by [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-subcanonical]. The base-change functor $u_{f_i}$ preserves finite limits and coverings [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image], and both sites are subcanonical, so [lem-pur-site-representable-algebraic-pullback] gives $f_i^{-1}h_{U_{ia}}\cong h_{u_{f_i}(U_{ia})}=h_{V_{ia}}$. An element of $h_{U_{ia}}(W)$ is an arrow $W\to U_{ia}$, so the element sites of the cited node are the localized sites $(S_i)_{\mathrm{proet}}/U_{ia}$ and $(X_i)_{\mathrm{proet}}/V_{ia}$, with the restricted rings of step 3; the inverse image of $(f_i)_A$, $(H\to A)\mapsto(f_i^{-1}H\to f_i^{-1}A)$, agrees with that of the localized morphism of step 3 by its canonical isomorphism $(f_V)^{-1}j_V^{-1}\cong j_U^{-1}f^{-1}$, and both structural ring maps are $c_{v_{ia}}$ there. The two-isomorphism transport of [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons] therefore identifies $L(f_i)_A^*$ with $P_{v_{ia}}$. The node gives $(P_{f_i}(i_i^*K))|_{V_{ia}}\simeq P_{v_{ia}}((i_i^*K)|_{U_{ia}})$, using the inverse of its displayed $\theta$. Combine this with step 4 and apply the functor $P_{v_{ia}}$ to the given chart isomorphism $(i_i^*K)|_{U_{ia}}\simeq B_{U_{ia}}\otimes_R L_{ia}^\bullet$. This proves the first local comparison in the statement. The cited slice theorem applies to unbounded complexes and arbitrary structural ring maps.

source.place: Tag 04IF, lemma-localize-morphism-ringed-topoi, with its ordinary unbounded derived slice comparison

proof.text: Fix one chart and abbreviate $U=U_{ia}$, $V=V_{ia}$, $L=L_{ia}^\bullet$. Put $M^q=B_U\otimes_R L^q$. Choose split maps $L^q\to R^{r_q}\to L^q$ whose composite is the identity, as allowed by finite projectivity. Tensoring these maps exhibits $M^q$ as a retract of $B_U^{r_q}$. For any exact sequence of $B_U$-module sheaves, tensoring with $B_U^{r_q}$ gives its finite direct sum, which is exact componentwise; tensoring with $M^q$ is the direct summand cut out by the displayed splitting, and kernels and images split along the two complementary projections. Thus it too is exact. This verifies flatness directly from [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]; no flatness over $R$ of $B_U$ is needed.

source.place: Tag 03ER, definition-flat, item (3); elementary split-summand argument

proof.text: The complex $M^\bullet=B_U\otimes_R L^\bullet$ is bounded, with flat terms by step 6, hence K-flat by [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site]. The computation counit of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback] therefore gives the canonical isomorphism $P_v[M^\bullet]\xrightarrow{\sim}[v_B^*M^\bullet]$. This is the specified ordinary derived computation counit, not an isomorphism obtained after completion. Its hypotheses concern the source complex, not flatness of $c_v$.

On a finite free module with basis $e_1,\ldots,e_r$, define the termwise comparison by
$$B_V\otimes_{v^{-1}B_U}v^{-1}(B_U^r)\longrightarrow B_V^r,\qquad b\otimes ae_j\longmapsto b\,c_v(a)e_j.$$
The inverse sends $be_j$ to $b\otimes e_j$; the balanced-tensor relations make the two composites identities. Here inverse image preserves the finite direct sum, as a left adjoint in [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image], and the displayed coefficient maps preserve the constant scalars from $R$ by their constant-section construction and all finite projections. For a finite projective summand represented by an idempotent matrix $e\in M_r(R)$, the same comparison intertwines $v^*(e)$ with $e$ on $B_V^r$, since it sends each constant entry to the same entry. Restrict the comparison and its inverse to this split summand. The formula commutes with every $R$-linear map between summands (apply the formula to its matrix between the chosen free modules), hence with each differential of $L$. Consequently it gives a complex isomorphism $v_B^*(B_U\otimes_R L^\bullet)\simeq B_V\otimes_R L^\bullet$. With step 7 this is the last asserted isomorphism, with exactly the basis and idempotent normalization required. The chart isomorphisms of step 5 now give all displayed conclusions.
